# Stack 03b — the canvas

**Waiting on Kent — nothing.** Every open item on this plan was answered on 2026-09-17. Three answers changed the design and are written into the body below: **provenance leaves the wire's stroke and becomes a three-step origin mark at the wire's tail**; **the diff view shows structure only until the engine's world route exists**, so there is no committed illustrative world and no "illustrative numbers" chip; and **the range under a number now means something specific** — how sure we are of the number, not how much the world can move — which the chip label, its hover sentence and the delta rail's new `agreement` column all have to say out loud (decision record 0014). The rest were accepted as written. Everything is marked **Kent, 2026-09-17** in the pre-decisions table.

---

**Goal:** the Hormuz map drawn so well that Kent wants to look at it. Tiles you can read, wires that show what kind of push they carry, a layout that never becomes a hairball, a panel that answers "why is this number what it is", and two worlds laid over each other so the change is obvious. Driven entirely by `GET /api/fixtures/hormuz`, which already works.

**What this stack must not do.** No model. No engine arithmetic — not one line that adds a strength, evaluates a shape or multiplies a likelihood. If the canvas needs a number, it comes over the wire from the fixture or, later, from stack 03a's world route. No backend files. No changes to `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` — that file belongs to stack 03a this cycle. No streaming (`spec/workbench/streaming-growth.md` is stack 04). No thesis card, no tail strip, no live prices.

**Rests on:** decision record 0007 (React Flow for the canvas, ELK for automatic layout, Motion for animation; own the look; no pop-ups), 0008 (the four testing layers). Read 0007's "Decision Outcome" — it is already a configuration list and this stack implements it.

**Read before writing a line of code:** `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` §7 in full, all fourteen items UX-1 to UX-14. `spec/vocabulary.md`, especially the **Interface words** table — the six buttons and their badges are copied from it word for word and nowhere else. Then `docs/research/03-ui-ux-directions.md` §2, §3 and §5 for craft, with one correction: **that report recommends its "Instrument" direction, and Kent rejected the recommendation.** The look is the *Workbench* — decision D3 in `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` §3: *the rigor of a visual-programming tool (boxes with typed sockets, wires that show the signal's shape) × cards rich with evidence you can pin and arrange like a mood board × a simulation game's sense of world state and time. Not minimalist; not a game.* The report's craft rules — typography, the two colour axes, the motion budget, the fourteen anti-patterns — all still apply.

**Runs in parallel with stack 03a (the engine).** Kent's decision D11.

---

## The four pull requests

Branch from `main`. Each pull request's base is the one above it.

| # | Branch → base | Contents |
|---|---------------|----------|
| 1 | `spec/03b-workbench` → `main` | **Docs only.** Six chapters: `spec/workbench/{tiles-ports-wires,layout-and-zoom,diff-view,inspector,color-motion-type,keyboard-and-access}.md`. Update the landing page's chapter table. **Amend `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` UX-6 and INV-12's row, and `spec/workbench/README.md`'s INV-12 row**, so provenance is carried by *a mark*, not *a stroke style* — see pull request 3. Three places, changed together. `streaming-growth.md` is stack 04 — do not write it |
| 2 | `feat/03b-canvas` → #1 | React Flow, the ELK worker, the custom tile, typed ports, the `WorldSource` seam, the launchpad. The Hormuz map draws |
| 3 | `feat/03b-wires` → #2 | Custom wires, the colour law and its tokens, the persistent Inspector, the path-product bar (INV-8) |
| 4 | `feat/03b-diff-and-keys` → #3 | Ghost overlay, delta rail, A ⇄ A′, the branch panel and UX-14, the keyboard map, reduced motion, the outline view, the end-to-end smoke test, the `e2e` job |

---

## Pull request 1 — the six chapters

Follow the chapter shape in `spec/README.md`: Purpose · Data model · Behaviour · INVARIANTS · ANTI-PATTERNS · Open questions. An interface chapter's "Data model" is the props a component takes and the tokens it reads; its "Behaviour" is worked examples on the Hormuz map. Every invariant names the test that checks it — a component test, or a line on the visual review checklist, which is itself a checkable thing.

The two invariants this part owns are **INV-8** (any displayed path shows the product of its link likelihoods beside the story) and **INV-12** (nothing is carried by hue alone: every direction has a glyph, every tail a texture, every provenance **a mark**). `keyboard-and-access.md` also owns the rendering rule that makes INV-7 visible: a chip never shows more than two significant figures and never omits its range.

`color-motion-type.md` carries **the colour law in one table**, and it is the chapter Kent will read first. Its organising rule is **one channel per meaning** — write that sentence into the chapter and into the writer's brief, because every failure in this area is two meanings fighting over one channel. The law: *likelihood rides brightness; direction of financial effect rides hue, blue up and amber down, always with a glyph and a sign; tail risk rides a hatch texture; **the kind of push rides the wire's stroke**; **provenance rides a mark at the wire's tail**; branch identity rides its own small palette and a name chip.*

**This refines two things already written, and pull request 1 must amend them rather than quietly diverge.** `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` UX-6 says "provenance → stroke style (`asserted` dashed)", its INV-12 row says "every provenance a stroke style", and `spec/workbench/README.md` repeats that wording. All three become **a mark**, because the stroke is now fully spent on the kind of push — a wire cannot be dot-dash for `impulse` and dashed for `argued` at the same time, and stack 02 already gave the stroke to the shape. The substance of UX-6 and INV-12 is unchanged: provenance is still visible on every wire, still without colour.

---

## Pull request 2 — canvas and tiles

**React Flow, and only its bare stylesheet.** `import "@xyflow/react/dist/base.css"` — never `style.css`, which carries the library's own look. A lint rule fails the `frontend` job if `style.css` appears anywhere (decision record 0007 promises this rule; write it).

**The tile.** A custom node type, **280 pixels wide**, height clamped, everything on the 8-pixel grid, hairline borders at 10% of the text colour, no shadows. It shows six things and no more:

1. The claim, wrapping to at most three lines then ellipsized — never truncated mid-word; the full text lives in the Inspector.
2. **Three belief chips** — model, user, market — as a three-up row. Each reads `.61 (.45–.75)`: two significant figures and the range, always. An empty `user` slot is a dash inviting a number. An empty `market` slot reads **no market** with its reason beside it, never a blank and never a placeholder number.

   **The range means one specific thing and the interface has to say which** (Kent, 2026-09-17, decision record 0014). It is *how sure we are of the number*, not *how much the world can move* — the second is already inside the likelihood. So the model chip's label is, word for word:

   > **model interval, uncalibrated** · how sure we are of `.35` — not how much the world can move

   and hovering it gives the sentence in full:

   > "Across 2 000 versions of this map — each one a set of numbers this model would have stood behind — the answer landed between .20 and .49 eight times in ten. Nobody has checked whether that 8-in-10 holds up; no claim on this map has resolved yet."

   Two things that sentence does on purpose: it says *eight times in ten* rather than naming a percentile, and it admits in its last clause that nothing is calibrated. Both are the product's honesty rule doing its job, and neither is optional.
3. Evidence clippings: at most two, each a letter monogram plus one line.
4. The resolve-by date.
5. A silhouette carrying `kind` — four of them, for `hypothesis`, `event`, `market`, `not_tradeable`. Shape carries the kind; hue never does.
6. Its badges, when it has any — see UX-14 in pull request 4.

**Typed ports.** One input group and one output group per tile, as React Flow handles. `trigger` and `sustain` wires attach to **distinct handle identifiers**, so what a wire means is visible at the socket before you follow it.

**ELK, off the main thread.** `elk.algorithm: layered`, `elk.direction: RIGHT`, `elk.layered.nodePlacement.strategy: NETWORK_SIMPLEX`, `elk.layered.crossingMinimization.semiInteractive: true`, `elk.layered.spacing.nodeNodeBetweenLayers: 120`, run in a Web Worker so layout never freezes the page. Already-placed tiles are pinned with `elk.position` so a later tile never reshuffles an earlier layer. `fitView` frames the map on first load only; after that `setCenter` follows the focused tile, because losing your place after a re-layout is anti-pattern 8 in the research. Cap seven tiles per layer and collapse the rest into a "+4 more" tile.

**Level of detail by zoom.** Below 0.6 zoom a tile becomes a summary — claim and belief chips only. Text never scales below 11 pixels; the tile changes representation instead of shrinking.

**Tiles do not drag.** Decision record 0007, and research anti-pattern 13: half-supported dragging looks broken. Pin, group and annotate arrive as explicit actions. Say so in the interface — a line in the keyboard sheet — rather than leaving a user to discover it by failing.

### The seam — `WorldSource`

Stack 03a is building the world route at the same time as this stack. The seam that keeps them apart:

```ts
export interface WorldSource {
  /** The base map and its branches, as the fixture route already serves them. */
  readBundle(id: string): Promise<FixtureBundle>;
  /** One world. Its numbers are OPTIONAL — see below. */
  readWorld(request: WorldRequest): Promise<WorldView>;
}
```

Two implementations. `FixtureWorldSource` reads `GET /api/fixtures/hormuz` and uses the fixture's stored `beliefs.model` for the base world — honest, because the fixture says in its own comments that those are illustrative. `ApiWorldSource` calls `POST /api/worlds` and `POST /api/worlds/diff`.

**And for the second world, before the engine exists, there is no second set of numbers at all** (Kent, 2026-09-17). No committed illustrative file, no hand-written likelihoods, no "illustrative numbers" chip. Numbers nobody computed are exactly the state a user cannot trace, and a plan that ships them for one stack ships them.

**What the diff view shows instead is structure, and structure is real.** It is computed from the branch — which this stack already has, because the fixture serves it — and it needs no arithmetic whatsoever:

| State | Computed from the branch by |
|---|---|
| `added` | The claim arrives in an `insert` |
| `killed` | The claim is the target of a `do(…, false)`, or the edits leave it with no path from the hypothesis |
| `downstream` | The claim is in the affected set of at least one edit — it is a claim your change can move |
| `untouched` | Everything else. Byte-identical, and the canvas can say so with confidence |

That is a genuinely useful view on its own: *"here is what your edit can reach, and here is what it provably cannot"* is the product's central correctness claim made visible, and it is the half of the diff that does not depend on the engine at all. Following arrows is **reachability, not arithmetic** — no strength is added, no likelihood is moved — so it does not break this stack's rule. When 03a lands, the server's `affected_set` is the authority and the browser's version becomes a hint that must agree with it; a component test pins the two against the Hormuz branch.

So every number slot in `WorldView` is optional, and an absent number **renders as an absence with a reason** — *"no engine yet"* in this stack, *"no market"* for an unpriced claim, a dash inviting your own number for an empty user slot. Never a blank, never a zero, never a placeholder. When 03a's route merges, switching to `ApiWorldSource` fills those slots and adds the fifth state, `shifted`; nothing is deleted, because nothing false was written.

`WorldView` is this stack's own view model in `frontend/src/world/types.ts`, written by hand — **not** generated from `schema.ts`, which belongs to stack 03a this cycle.

**The launchpad.** The empty state, and no illustration: the four example hypotheses from `ASSIGNMENT.md` as one-click cards, plus the Explore / Verify pair visible and explained in one line each. Only the Hormuz card opens a map in this stack; the other three say what they will do and are visibly not yet live — never silently inert.

## Pull request 3 — wires, the colour law, the Inspector

**Wires are custom edges**, drawn with `getSmoothStepPath` and a midpoint chip through `EdgeLabelRenderer`. **The stroke says one thing and one thing only: what kind of push this is** (Kent, 2026-09-17). Five encodings, each readable without colour:

| What | How |
|---|---|
| Signal shape | Stroke pattern: `impulse` dot-dash · `step` solid · `ramp` a gradient along the stroke |
| Strength | Stroke width, from `|strength|`, regardless of sign. Four steps, not a continuous ramp |
| `sustain` versus `trigger` | A `sustain` wire is double-stroked. A `trigger` wire is single |
| `reflexive` | The wire loops back on itself and carries a **lag chip** reading the delay in days |
| Provenance | **An origin mark at the wire's tail**, where the arrow leaves its cause — not the stroke. Three steps: **●●●** `documented`, `historical`, `market_implied` · **●●** `argued`, `user` · **●** `asserted`, `simulated`. The exact word is in the Inspector |

**Why provenance left the stroke.** One channel cannot carry two meanings. The stroke already says `impulse` or `step` or `ramp`, and stack 02 gave it that job; asking it to also say `argued` or `documented` means a dot-dash-and-dashed wire that says neither clearly. A three-step mark at the tail says the useful thing at a glance — *is there a document behind this, or is it the model talking* — and the seven-way distinction, which nobody reads off a picture anyway, lives in the Inspector where there is room for the word. Build it as one small component, `OriginMark`, used by the wire and by the Inspector so the two can never disagree. INV-12 still holds: provenance is visible on every wire and no hue is involved.

**The midpoint chip** shows the conditional likelihood in the arrow-and-bar idiom the forecasting site Metaculus uses: the target's likelihood **with this arrow's source supposed true**. That number is **not computed here** and it is **not on the world** — stack 03a computes it lazily, one arrow at a time, through `POST /api/worlds/conditional`, because computing all of them costs a whole extra propagation per arrow. So the canvas asks for it when a wire is hovered or selected and caches the answer. Until it has one — and always, in this stack, since the route does not exist yet — the chip shows the arrow's push read back in words, *"+1.6 · a strong push toward"*, which is data already on the link and needs no arithmetic. **Never a guessed number.**

**The colour law**, in one place, as CSS custom properties added to `frontend/src/styles/tokens.css` under a clearly marked new block. No existing token changes value.

| Axis | Channel | Tokens |
|---|---|---|
| Likelihood | Brightness — a five-step luminance ramp | `--p-0` … `--p-4`, each with its contrast ratio in a comment, as every existing token has |
| Direction of financial effect | Hue **plus a glyph plus a sign**, never hue alone | `--dir-up` (blue, ▲) and `--dir-down` (amber, ▼), both already in `tokens.css` |
| Tail risk | Texture | `--tail`, the hatch already in `tokens.css` |
| The kind of push | Stroke pattern, width and doubling | `impulse` dot-dash · `step` solid · `ramp` gradient; width from `|strength|`; `sustain` doubled |
| Provenance | **A mark, not a stroke** | The three-step origin mark at the wire's tail, above (Kent, 2026-09-17) |
| Branch identity | Its own small palette, on lanes and chips only — never on a tile's meaning | Violet, teal, rose, slate (*decided here*, accepted 2026-09-17). **Not amber**: amber already means "downward", and one hue cannot mean two things |

**The hover lens.** Hovering a tile dims everything not on its ancestor-or-descendant path to 15%. The research calls this the single highest-value interaction for legibility, and it is four lines of state.

**The Inspector is a persistent side panel and there are no pop-ups** (UX-10). It shows, for a claim: the full text, the resolution criteria and adjudicating source, the resolve-by date, the base rate with its reference class and its `k` of `n`, all three beliefs with owners, the evidence list, and — when the world carries one — the decomposition that makes the number explicable: *prior, then one line per incoming arrow with its push and its reason, then the result.* `spec/graph/belief.md` §B4 draws that block; copy its layout. **Reserve a slot directly under the range for "why is this band wide?"** — the answer is one sentence naming the claim whose own prior explains most of it (*"92% of this band is B's own starting number; pin that down and the band goes from 29 points to 8"*), it is computed from `World.range_shares`, and **it ships in stack 06, not here.** Leave the slot, leave a comment naming `range_shares`, render nothing. For an arrow: the rationale, the strength read back in words ("+1.6 — a strong push toward"), the mode in words, the lag, the shape, the sources with the day each was fetched, and the provenance in full — the word, with the same `OriginMark` the wire draws, so the mark and the word are one component and cannot drift apart.

**The path-product bar (INV-8).** Select a claim and a bar shows the multiplied-out likelihood of the path from the hypothesis to it, beside the story sentence. The product arrives on the world; this stack renders it. If it is absent, the bar says "no path shown" — it never multiplies anything itself.

## Pull request 4 — two worlds, the branch panel, the keyboard

**The ghost overlay.** Lay out the union of both worlds **once**, then draw the new world at full opacity and the old at 20% opacity, dashed, in the same coordinates. One layout, two paintings.

Each tile carries a diff state and that state drives its styling. In this stack there are four, all computed from the branch: `added` is solid with an accent ring; `killed` is ghosted, struck through, desaturated; **`downstream`** is drawn live — the claim your edit can reach, its number slot reading *"no engine yet"*; `untouched` is neutral, and it is the state the canvas can assert with confidence, because locality is a proven property and not a guess. The fifth state, `shifted` — `.61 → .18` with a directional chevron — arrives with the engine and needs no other change. **Never animate the diff as a crossfade** — `Space` toggles A ⇄ A′ as a hard switch, and the transition is scrubbable.

**The delta rail** sits beside the canvas. With the engine it is the terminal changes, ranked, one line each — *"the Polymarket Brent contract · .61 → .18 ▼ · largest on Oct 9"* — in the order the engine gave them, with **two columns that are never folded into the rank**: `range_width` (how unsure we are of the number) and **`agreement`** (the share of the 2 000 versions of the map that moved the same way — the vocabulary's reserved word for a number computed from how far independent runs differed, never self-reported). They answer different questions and a trader weighs them separately, which is why they are columns. Before the engine lands, **both columns render as an absence with its reason**, like every other number slot in this stack. **This stack does not rank and does not compute**: until the engine lands, the rail lists the terminals your edit can reach, in map order, each with an absence and a reason where the number will go. A rail that invented an ordering would be inventing the one thing the rail exists to tell you.

**UX-14, the overridden assertion.** A claim the user supposed true and that a later edit pushed back down never renders as plainly true. Its tile carries both states in order:

> **Supposed · Oct 1 → Retracted · Oct 2 · by "a confirmed military strike on Iranian territory"**

**While a claim is supposed, its tile shows the word where a likelihood would go** — *Supposed · Oct 1*, not `1.0` and not `.98`. The engine treats a supposition as a hard fact in every draw (stack 03a, Kent's decision of 2026-09-17), so there is no number to show, and inventing one would answer a question the user did not ask.

Its series then carries three named states after that, and the tile and the time axis both read them: **supposed** → **withdrawn** (the supposition has been undermined and no opposing push has arrived yet — labelled *"withdrawn — no live push yet"*) → **pushed**. On the Hormuz branch that is Oct 1 supposed, Oct 2 to Oct 4 withdrawn at `.35`, Oct 5 onward pushed to about `.07`. The three-day gap between the badge's date and the day the number moves is the honest shape of the answer, and the interface must be able to say so rather than smoothing it away.

Every part of that line is data on the world, not inference: the assignment gives *Supposed* and its date; the retraction gives the date, the arrow and the claim to name; `states` gives the three-state series. The **branch panel** lists that branch's edits in the order they were made, each with the badge its operation earns, so the surprising rule reads as a sequence rather than as a number that moved on its own.

**The six buttons and badges, word for word from `spec/vocabulary.md`'s Interface words table** — copy them, do not paraphrase, and never show a code name:

| Button | Badge afterwards |
|---|---|
| **Suppose this is true** (and **Suppose this is false**) | **Supposed · date** |
| **This happened** | **Happened · date** |
| **Add a claim** (hinted "…but this also happens") | **Added** |
| **Change this push** | **Retuned** |
| **Split this claim** | **Split** |
| **My own number** | none — the three-up belief chip is the badge |

and the derived one no button produces: **Retracted · date · by "…"**.

In this stack the buttons **build a branch and show it**; they do not move a number, because moving numbers is the engine's job. **My own number** and **Change this push** append an edit to the branch and the branch panel shows it immediately. **Split this claim** is visibly not yet live and says so (stack 06).

**The keyboard map (UX-9).** `⌘K` command palette · `j`/`k` between siblings · `h`/`l` along wires between layers — arrow movement follows the *wires*, not screen space · `E` intervene · `B` branch · `Space` A ⇄ A′ · `?` the shortcuts sheet. Focus is always visible, using `--focus`. Everything reachable by keyboard alone, end to end.

**Reduced motion (UX-7).** The motion budget is three animations and no more: the propagation wave (wires draw in causal order, about 200 milliseconds, staggered 60 milliseconds down the map), branch creation, and the belief number-roll. Everything else is at most 120 milliseconds of opacity. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the **ordering survives and the tweening goes** — per-layer instant reveals, a number swap instead of a roll, a hard cut instead of a ghost transition. Never remove the ordering: the ordering is the causality.

**The outline view (UX-12).** The map also exists as a nested list with `role="tree"`, each item read as a sentence — *"Brent crude settles below $68 for five sessions, 61 per cent likely, caused by the war-risk premium falling"*. A re-propagation announces itself through `aria-live="polite"`: *"Branch created. Six claims changed, one retracted."*

**Tests** (decision record 0008, layer 4):

- `frontend/src/graph/__tests__/layout.test.ts` — pinned tiles keep their positions across an incremental layout; the union layout used for a diff is stable.
- `frontend/src/graph/__tests__/diffState.test.ts` — the reducer maps a base map plus a branch to the four structural states, and the claim the strike branch provably cannot reach comes out `untouched`.
- `frontend/src/world/__tests__/branchReducer.test.ts` — the intervention panel appends edits in order and never edits one in place.
- `frontend/src/components/__tests__/beliefChip.test.tsx` — **`test_chip_never_shows_more_than_two_significant_figures`**, that the range is never omitted, that an absent number renders its reason, and that a supposed claim renders the word rather than a likelihood. This is decision record 0005's promised frontend rendering test; it is the one test that holds NFR-1 up.
- One end-to-end browser test with Playwright: open the Hormuz map, the tiles draw, open the strike branch, downstream tiles change and the fully separated claim does not, and H's tile reads *Supposed · Oct 1 → Retracted · Oct 2 · by "…"*.
- A fifth continuous-integration job, `e2e`, running that one test. **No API key in it** (INV-13).

Everything else is disjoint: 03b is `frontend/**` plus `spec/workbench/**` plus `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; 03a is `backend/**` plus `spec/multiverse/**`.

### The brief every agent gets

Same nine parts as the engine stack, with four differences:

1. **The two vetoes are the point of this stack**, not a footnote. Paste them and paste D3's sentence about what the Workbench is.
2. **Read first:** `AGENTS.md`; this plan's section for your pull request; decision record 0007; `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` §7 in full; `spec/vocabulary.md` including the Interface words table; `spec/workbench/README.md`; `docs/research/03-ui-ux-directions.md` §2, §3, §5 — **with the correction that the report's "Instrument" recommendation was rejected.**
3. **Verify before reporting:** `npm run check`, then use the `run` skill to launch the app and **capture screenshots of every state you built** — empty, loaded, hovered, selected, diffed, keyboard-focused, reduced-motion, light theme. Attach the file paths to your report. An agent that reports "it looks good" without pictures has not finished.
4. **The pre-decisions table above, pasted in full.**

### The coordinator's review, after every agent

- [ ] `git diff --stat` against the owned-files list; **no `schema.ts` diff, no `backend/` diff**
- [ ] `npm run check` run by me in the worktree
- [ ] `package.json` diff read: no dependency beyond the four named above
- [ ] Launch the app myself and walk every state — do not review from the agent's screenshots alone
- [ ] Run the veto checks below
- [ ] Read every string on screen against `spec/vocabulary.md`; no code name, no internal number, no jargon
- [ ] Commit messages: type, scope, co-author line
- [ ] Write the pull request body (*What* · *Which invariant it satisfies* · *What is deliberately not here*); open with `gh pr create --base <parent>`
- [ ] Append `STATUS.md`

### The veto checks — run these on every screenshot

Kent vetoes a template-looking interface on sight, so the coordinator looks for the template first.

1. Does anything look like a component library's defaults — a rounded blue button, a drop shadow, a system font stack, a default focus ring?
2. Is there a spinner anywhere? A pop-up? A dialog you have to dismiss? Any of the three is a veto.
3. **Convert the screenshot to greyscale.** Does every arrow still say what kind it is and where it came from, every direction still read up or down, every tail still show as texture? If not, INV-12 is broken.
4. Is any number on screen showing more than two significant figures, or missing its range?
5. Is there a number whose origin cannot be named in one click? Is there a number nobody computed — an empty slot filled in rather than left as an absence with a reason?
6. Is the map layered left to right, or is it a hairball with crossings?
7. Is any text below 11 pixels? Is any text under 4.5 to 1 contrast, in either theme?
8. Is the tile 280 pixels wide and on the 8-pixel grid? Measure it, do not eyeball it.
9. Tab through the whole screen with the keyboard only: is focus always visible, and does arrow movement follow the wires?
10. Turn on reduced motion: is the ordering still there and the tweening gone?
11. Are the six buttons and badges word for word the Interface words table?
12. Does a claim that was supposed and then overridden say so on its tile?

### The gate

**M3b** — stack 03b complete: four pull requests open and green; the Hormuz map draws, wires carry their five encodings, the Inspector answers "why", two worlds lay over each other, UX-14 renders, the keyboard works end to end, the `e2e` job is green. Kent has looked at it and nothing triggered a veto.

**M3** is both gates: the engine computes it and the canvas shows it. Stack 04 joins them by switching `WorldSource` to `ApiWorldSource`, which fills the empty number slots and adds the fifth diff state. Nothing is deleted at that point, because nothing false was written.

1	# The diff view — two worlds in one picture
2	
3	## Purpose
4	
5	You supposed the strait reopens. Then you added a strike the next day. Two maps now exist, and one
6	question matters: **what did my edit reach, and what did it provably leave alone?**
7	
8	The diff view answers it in one picture. Both maps are laid out **once**, together, then painted
9	twice in the same coordinates — the new world solid, the old world faint behind it. Nothing moves
10	between them, so every difference you see is a real difference and not a re-layout.
11	
12	Before the engine exists that answer is **structural** — *here is what your edit can reach, and here
13	is what it cannot* — and where a number will later sit, this stack draws **an absence with its
14	reason**: never a blank, never a zero, never a stand-in.
15	
16	This chapter owns the ghost overlay, the delta rail, the A ⇄ A′ toggle and the branch panel — and,
17	because every number slot on the world uses them, the `Known<T>` and `Absence` shapes the whole of
18	`spec/workbench/` reads.
19	
20	---
21	
22	## Data model
23	
24	### The seam — `WorldSource`
25	
26	The engine (stack 03a) and the canvas (this stack) are built at the same time. One interface keeps
27	them apart, and it is the only place the canvas learns anything:
28	
29	```ts
30	export interface WorldSource {
31	  /** The base map and its branches, as the fixture route already serves them. */
32	  readBundle(id: string): Promise<FixtureBundle>;
33	  /** One world. Its numbers are OPTIONAL — see `Known<T>` below. */
34	  readWorld(request: WorldRequest): Promise<WorldView>;
35	}
36	```
37	
38	Two implementations, and the screen cannot tell which it has. `FixtureWorldSource` reads
39	`GET /api/fixtures/hormuz` and uses the fixture's stored `beliefs.model` for the **base** world —
40	honest, because the fixture says in its own comments that those are illustrative. `ApiWorldSource`
41	calls `POST /api/worlds` and `POST /api/worlds/diff` once they exist.
42	
43	**For the second world, before the engine, there is no second set of numbers at all.** No committed
44	illustrative world, no hand-written likelihoods, no "illustrative numbers" chip. A number nobody
45	computed is exactly the state a reader cannot trace.
46	
47	### `WorldView` — this stack's own view model
48	
49	`WorldView` lives in `frontend/src/world/types.ts` and is **written by hand**, not generated from
50	`frontend/src/api/schema.ts`, which belongs to stack 03a this cycle. Three kinds of absence need
51	three different sentences, so an absence carries both its kind and its sentence:
52	
53	```ts
54	/** A value we may not have. Never a blank, never a zero, never a placeholder. */
55	export type Known<T> =
56	  | { known: true; value: T }
57	  | { known: false; absence: Absence };
58	
59	export interface Absence {
60	  /** Which absence this is; it picks the words. */
61	  kind: "no_engine" | "no_market" | "not_said";
62	  /** The sentence shown beside the words. Always present, never empty. */
63	  reason: string;
64	}
65	
66	/** `killed` is forced false, full stop. `shifted` needs two numbers, so it arrives with the
67	    engine and is never produced here. */
68	export type DiffState = "added" | "killed" | "downstream" | "untouched" | "shifted";
69	
70	/** `branchId: null` is the base world, the empty branch; the seed makes a world replay. */
71	export interface WorldRequest { baseId: string; branchId: string | null; seed?: number }
72	
73	export interface WorldView {
74	  baseId: string;
75	  branchId: string | null;
76	  claims: ClaimView[];
77	  links: LinkView[];
78	  terminals: DeltaRow[];        // what the delta rail draws
79	  headline: Known<string>;      // the one-line plain-English diff (FR-16)
80	  /** How many versions of the map the engine ran to produce these numbers.
81	      Absent when nothing was computed — which is what picks the chip's sentence. */
82	  versions?: number;
83	}
84	
85	/** One claim as this stack reads it. `TileProps` and `ClaimDetail` are projections of it. */
86	export interface ClaimView {
87	  id: string;
88	  claim: string;                                                  // the full sentence
89	  kind: "hypothesis" | "event" | "market" | "not_tradeable";
90	  resolution: { criteria: string; source: string; by: string };   // all three required (INV-1)
91	  prior: BeliefView;
92	  baseRate: Known<BaseRateView>;
93	  beliefs: { model: Known<BeliefView>; user: Known<BeliefView>; market: Known<BeliefView> };
94	  evidence: readonly EvidenceView[];
95	  diff: DiffState;
96	  badges: readonly Badge[];              // Supposed · date, Added, Retracted · date · by "…"
97	  states: Known<readonly SeriesState[]>; // supposed → withdrawn → pushed, with dates
98	  decomposition: Known<Decomposition>;   // prior, a line per incoming arrow, the result
99	  pathProduct: Known<PathProduct>;       // INV-8; computed on the world, never here
100	  rangeShares?: Record<string, number>;  // stack 06 — nothing reads it yet
101	}
102	
103	/** One arrow as this stack reads it. `WireProps` and `LinkDetail` are projections of it. */
104	export interface LinkView {
105	  id: string; source: string; target: string;
106	  mode: "trigger" | "sustain";
107	  strength: number;                      // signed; on the log-odds scale
108	  lag: number;                           // days
109	  shape: "impulse" | "step" | "ramp";
110	  halfLife: number | null;               // impulse only
111	  reflexive: boolean;                    // a feedback arrow: a market acting back on the world
112	  rationale: string;
113	  sources: readonly { url: string; title: string; retrieved: Known<string> }[];
114	  provenance: "documented" | "historical" | "market_implied"
115	            | "argued" | "user" | "asserted" | "simulated";
116	  conditional: Known<BeliefView>;        // the midpoint chip; fetched one arrow at a time
117	}
118	
119	export interface DeltaRow {
120	  claimId: string;
121	  label: string;                                     // the terminal's own words
122	  move: Known<{ from: number; to: number; largestOn: string }>;
123	  rangeWidth: Known<number>;   // "how firm": the width of the new world's own range on this claim
124	  agreement: Known<number>;    // "same direction": the share of versions that moved the same way
125	}
126	```
127	
128	Every number slot is `Known<T>`, so an absent number **cannot** be rendered as anything but its
129	reason — a type-level guarantee, not a convention.
130	
131	**`BeliefView`** — one likelihood with its range and a name on it — is defined once in
132	[`tiles-ports-wires.md`](tiles-ports-wires.md), because the belief chip is the only component that
133	takes one. `TileProps` and `WireProps` there, and `ClaimDetail` and `LinkDetail` in
134	[`inspector.md`](inspector.md), are projections of `ClaimView` and `LinkView` above.
135	
136	**One field, two spellings, said once here.** The server's wire name is `range_width`; the view
137	model's is `rangeWidth`. Same number, and neither is ever shown — the rail's column is headed **how
138	firm**. Likewise the field `agreement`, whose column reads **same direction**: the bare word
139	*agreement* is left free on screen for stack 04's run-to-run number.
140	
141	### Component props
142	
143	```ts
144	interface GhostOverlayProps {
145	  now: WorldView; before: WorldView;   // A′ painted solid; A painted faint and dashed
146	  positions: PositionMap;              // the union layout, computed once
147	  showing: "now" | "before";           // which one Space last selected
148	}
149	interface DeltaRailProps  { rows: DeltaRow[]; ranked: boolean }   // ranked is false in this stack
150	interface BranchPanelProps { branch: BranchView; onEdit: (edit: Intervention) => void }  // appends
151	```
152	
153	`PositionMap` is defined in [`layout-and-zoom.md`](layout-and-zoom.md), which owns layout.
154	
155	**Tokens read:** `--surface`, `--surface-raised`, `--hairline`, `--text`, `--text-muted`,
156	`--accent`, `--focus`, `--font-mono` for every number, `--space-1` … `--space-4`, the likelihood
157	ramp `--p-0` … `--p-4`, and the branch palette — violet, teal, rose, slate. All are defined in
158	[`color-motion-type.md`](color-motion-type.md); this chapter defines no token and changes none. A
159	direction, once the engine lands, is rendered through `DirectionReadout`, which owns those tokens.
160	
161	---
162	
163	## Behaviour
164	
165	Worked on the Hormuz map (the cast is in [`README.md`](README.md)). This chapter uses all seven base
166	claims, and the branch `br_hormuz_then_strike`: suppose **H** true on Oct 1; add **S** *a confirmed
167	military strike on Iranian territory* with three arrows (S → B, S → C, S → H); suppose S true on
168	Oct 2. The map's "today" is 2026-10-01.
169	
170	### B1 — One layout, two paintings
171	
172	Lay out the union of both worlds **once**. Every claim in both gets one position. Then paint twice
173	into that one coordinate space: **A′** at full opacity and solid, **A** at **20%** opacity, dashed,
174	behind it. Nothing shifts and nothing fades into anything, so a tile in the same place in both
175	paintings really is the same claim. On Hormuz the union is eight tiles — the seven base claims plus
176	S, the only one with nothing behind it.
177	
178	The hover lens *multiplies* that 20% rather than replacing it
179	([`tiles-ports-wires.md`](tiles-ports-wires.md)), so a tile that is both off the hovered path and
180	old lands near 3% and disappears — which is correct: you asked to see one path in one world.
181	
182	### B2 — The four structural states, computed from the branch
183	
184	Each tile carries a diff state and the state drives how it is drawn. In this stack there are four,
185	and **every one is computed from the branch alone**:
186	
187	| State | Computed from the branch by | Drawn as |
188	|---|---|---|
189	| `added` | The claim arrives in an `insert` | Solid, with an accent ring |
190	| `killed` | The claim is the target of a **Suppose this is false** — full stop | Ghosted, struck through, desaturated |
191	| `downstream` | The claim is in the affected set of at least one edit — a claim your change **can** move | Drawn live, its number slot reading *"no engine yet"* |
192	| `untouched` | Everything else. Byte-identical, and the canvas can say so without hedging | Neutral |
193	
194	**`killed` means forced false and nothing else** (Kent, 2026-09-17). "No path from the hypothesis
195	reaches this claim any more" is a fact about a *route*, not a state of a claim, and the Inspector's
196	path bar reports it in those words. No claim is ever **only in A**, either, because no edit removes
197	one. Nothing in the Hormuz bundle supposes a claim false, so `killed` is drawn but not exercised by
198	the worked example; a unit test over a hand-built branch covers it.
199	
200	**Following arrows is reachability, not arithmetic** — no strength is added, no likelihood is
201	moved, no shape is evaluated. Which claims each operation reaches, and which arrows count, are both
202	settled in [`../multiverse/interventions.md`](../multiverse/interventions.md): the affected-set
203	table, and one named rule — *the map the engine works through is the map with feedback arrows set
204	aside*. Anything asking **what can move** reads that map, these diff states included; anything
205	asking **what can I walk to** reads the whole map — the hover lens, `h`/`l`, the outline.
206	
207	On the strike branch: **S** is `added`; **H** is `downstream`, because S → H was inserted *after*
208	the supposition on H and so is live; **C** and **B** are `downstream` from H and again directly from
209	S; **N1** through H → N1; **M1** and **M2** from B. And, as a consequence of that rule:
210	
211	> **R — *OPEC+ announces output restraint* — is `untouched`. Nothing on this branch can reach it.**
212	
213	R's only incoming arrow is B → R, the **feedback** arrow — a price outcome acting back on what
214	producers do. Set aside, R has no incoming arrow at all: an ancestor of B, never a descendant of
215	anything this branch touches. So the screen can say out loud: *your strike moves the oil price, the
216	insurance premium, both contracts and the diplomatic ending — and it cannot move OPEC's
217	announcement.* That sentence is the product, and `INV-workbench.41` and `.42` below pin it.
218	
219	### B3 — The fifth state arrives with the engine, and nothing is deleted
220	
221	`shifted` — `.61 → .18` with a directional chevron — needs two numbers to compare, so it cannot
222	exist here. When `ApiWorldSource` is switched on in stack 04 the empty slots fill and `shifted`
223	appears. **Nothing written in this stack is deleted then, because nothing false was written.** The
224	authority changes hands: the server's `affected_set` becomes the truth and the browser's structural
225	states become a **hint that must agree with it**, pinned by a component test on the Hormuz branch. A
226	browser quietly disagreeing with the engine about what an edit reached is the traceability veto
227	wearing a disguise.
228	
229	### B4 — A ⇄ A′ is a hard switch, never a crossfade
230	
231	`Space` swaps which world is solid — an instant switch, not a fade. Two half-drawn worlds on top of
232	each other is a picture of nothing, and a crossfade invites the eye to read the blur as a number
233	moving. The transition is **scrubbable**: sit on either side, go back and forth, and the map never
234	re-lays-out. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` there is nothing to remove, because there was
235	never a tween.
236	
237	### B5 — The delta rail, before the engine and after
238	
239	The rail sits beside the canvas and lists what changed at the **endings** — the claims that name an
240	instrument, or name why there is none. **With the engine** it is the terminal changes, ranked, one
241	line each, in the order the engine gave them:
242	
243	> the Polymarket Brent contract · `.61 → .18` ▼ · largest on Oct 9
244	
245	That order is the size of the move times the **weakest arrow on the best-backed route** from any of
246	the branch's edits to that ending — the route whose weakest arrow is strongest. Two factors and no
247	more; the engine computes it, the rail renders it in the order given, and beside it sit **two
248	columns that are never folded into the rank**:
249	
250	| Column on screen | The question it answers | Field |
251	|---|---|---|
252	| **how firm** | *How firm is this number?* The width of the new world's own range on that claim — the same quantity the tile shows, so the rail and the tile cannot disagree | `rangeWidth` |
253	| **same direction** | *Did it point the same way whatever numbers we started from?* The share of the 2 000 versions of the map that moved in the same direction | `agreement` |
254	
255	Different questions, weighed separately by a trader, which is why they are columns and not one
256	score. Folding width into the rank would sink exactly the claims that most deserve attention.
257	
258	**Before the engine — this stack — the rail does not rank and does not compute.** It lists the
259	terminals the edit can reach, in **map order**, each with an absence and a reason where the number
260	will go:
261	
262	```
263	                                                   change          how firm   same direction
264	M1  Polymarket "Brent below $70 on 2026-10-31"     no engine yet   —          —
265	M2  XLE underperforms SPY by more than 3%          no engine yet   —          —
266	N1  Omani-mediated talks resume                    no engine yet   —          —
267	```
268	
269	Each dash carries the same reason as the change beside it: no engine yet. All three endings are
270	reachable here, so all three are listed; R is not a terminal and never appears. **A rail that
271	invented an ordering would be inventing the one thing the rail exists to tell you** — map order is
272	visibly arbitrary and says so; a fabricated ranking looks like an answer.
273	
274	**The one-line summary above the rail** (FR-16) has a fixed second form for the case where the rail
275	has nothing to report: *"<edit> moves no ending and leaves <n> claims untouched."* Both forms are
276	sentences the world carries. Before the engine the summary is an absence with its reason, like every
277	other computed thing on this screen.
278	
279	### B6 — UX-14: an assertion a later edit overrode says so
280	
281	A claim the user supposed true, and that a later edit in the same branch pushed back down, is
282	**never drawn as plainly true**. H's tile carries both states in order, word for word:
283	
284	> **Supposed · Oct 1 → Retracted · Oct 2 · by "a confirmed military strike on Iranian territory"**
285	
286	**While a claim is supposed, its tile shows the word where a likelihood would go** — *Supposed ·
287	Oct 1*, not `1.0` and not `.98`. A supposition is a hard fact in every simulated world while it
288	holds, so there is no number to show, and inventing one answers a question nobody asked.
289	
290	After the retraction the claim passes through three named states. **Every part of the line and the
291	series is data, never inference** — and this stack has some of it and not the rest:
292	
293	| Part | On Hormuz | Comes from | Needs the world? |
294	|---|---|---|---|
295	| **Supposed · Oct 1** | Oct 1; H shows the word, not a number | The assignment itself: an earlier supposition on H, with its date | **No** — the branch carries it |
296	| **Retracted · Oct 2 · by "…"** | Oct 2 | A `sustain` arrow into H inserted afterwards, and the later edit that makes its source true; the quoted words are S's own `claim` field | **No** — structure and dates, the same reachability the four states use |
297	| **withdrawn** | Oct 2 – Oct 4, `.35`, labelled *"withdrawn — no live push yet"* | The `states` series: the cause of the opposing arrow became true on the 2nd, so we stop taking the user's word; S → H's three-day delay has not run | **Yes** |
298	| **pushed** | Oct 5 onward, about `.070` | The `states` series: the delay has run and S → H's −1.9 push lands on the prior | **Yes** |
299	
300	So in this stack H's tile carries the badge pair and its order, its number slot reads *"no engine
301	yet"*, and the series is absent with its reason. As with the affected set, the browser's derived
302	badge becomes a hint the world must agree with once the engine lands. (`.070`, not `.07`: two
303	significant figures on every number, the rule [`keyboard-and-access.md`](keyboard-and-access.md)
304	owns.)
305	
306	**The three-day gap between the badge's date and the day the number moves is honest, not something
307	to smooth away.** A supposition ends the day its undermining *cause* becomes true, not the day that
308	arrow's push arrives — otherwise "do I still take your word for this" would hang on a delay
309	parameter, and changing a lag from three days to thirty would let the supposition outlive the news
310	(decision record 0014).
311	
312	### B7 — The branch panel: a sequence, not a surprise
313	
314	The panel lists that branch's edits **in the order they were made**, each with the badge its
315	operation earns. Read as a sequence, the rule that a later addition outranks an earlier supposition
316	is obvious; met as a number that moved on its own, it reads as a bug.
317	
318	```
319	Hormuz opens, then Iran is struck                        ● violet
320	 1  The Strait of Hormuz reopens…                        Supposed · Oct 1
321	 2  A confirmed military strike on Iranian territory.    Added
322	 3  A confirmed military strike on Iranian territory.    Supposed · Oct 2
323	```
324	
325	**The six buttons and their badges**, copied word for word from
326	[`../vocabulary.md`](../vocabulary.md)'s *Interface words* table — copy, never paraphrase:
327	
328	| Code name (never on screen) | The button | The badge afterwards |
329	|---|---|---|
330	| `do` | **Suppose this is true** (and **Suppose this is false**) | **Supposed · date** |
331	| `observe` | **This happened** | **Happened · date** |
332	| `insert` | **Add a claim**, hinted as "…but this also happens" | **Added** |
333	| `retune` | **Change this push** | **Retuned** |
334	| `refine` | **Split this claim** | **Split** |
335	| `believe` | **My own number** | none — the three-up belief chip is the badge |
336	
337	And one derived badge no button produces: **Retracted · date · by "…"**. The six code names live in
338	the code, the wire format and the spec, and **none of them ever appears on screen**.
339	
340	Three rules in this stack:
341	
342	1. **The buttons build a branch and show it. They do not move a number.** **My own number** and
343	   **Change this push** append an edit and the panel shows it immediately; the likelihood slots stay
344	   as they were, reading their absence.
345	2. **Split this claim** is **visibly not yet live** and says so (stack 06). Never silently inert.
346	3. **Edits are appended, never edited in place.** The branch is the audit trail, and an audit trail
347	   you can edit is not one.
348	
349	---
350	
351	## INVARIANTS
352	
353	Each is *for all X, statement P holds*, and each names what checks it: a component test, or a
354	numbered line of the **visual review checklist** in [`README.md`](README.md). Frontend test names
355	are `test_snake_case`. Short file names below: **diffState** is
356	`frontend/src/graph/__tests__/diffState.test.ts`, **deltaRail**
357	`frontend/src/components/__tests__/deltaRail.test.tsx`, **ghostOverlay**
358	`frontend/src/components/__tests__/ghostOverlay.test.tsx`. This chapter uses `INV-workbench.40` …
359	`.49`.
360	
361	**INV-workbench.40 — one layout, two paintings.** For every claim present in both worlds, its
362	position in the A painting equals its position in the A′ painting, and toggling A ⇄ A′ changes no
363	position anywhere. That the union layout is itself stable is
364	[`layout-and-zoom.md`](layout-and-zoom.md)'s. *Tests:* ghostOverlay ›
365	`test_paints_both_worlds_from_one_position_map`, `test_space_changes_no_position`.
366	
367	**INV-workbench.41 — every diff state is derived, never assigned.** For every claim in a branch
368	world, its `DiffState` is a function of the base map and the branch's edits alone: no component sets
369	a state and no state is read from a number. *Test:* diffState ›
370	`test_computes_the_four_structural_states_for_the_strike_branch`.
371	
372	**INV-workbench.42 — what an edit cannot reach is said so.** For every claim outside the affected
373	set of every edit in the branch, the state is `untouched`. On the Hormuz strike branch that set is
374	exactly `{R}`. *Tests:* diffState › `test_r_comes_out_untouched`; `frontend/e2e/hormuz.spec.ts` ›
375	`test_the_fully_separated_claim_does_not_change`.
376	
377	**INV-workbench.43 — the browser never out-votes the engine.** For the Hormuz branch, every state
378	the browser computed equals the state derived from the server's `affected_set`. Both read the map
379	with feedback arrows set aside, which is why they can agree at all; the day stack 06 unrolls them,
380	`test_a_feedback_arrow_never_carries_a_change` in the domain fails loudly and points at the one
381	sentence to change. Until stack 03a lands this test is skipped with its reason written in it, never
382	deleted. *Test:* diffState › `test_agrees_with_the_servers_affected_set`.
383	
384	**INV-workbench.44 — `shifted` is never produced without two numbers.** For every pair of worlds in
385	which either side's likelihood is absent, no claim is `shifted`. *Test:* diffState ›
386	`test_never_shifts_on_an_absent_number`.
387	
388	**INV-workbench.45 — no number slot is ever blank.** For every claim and every delta row in this
389	view, a slot without a value renders its `Absence.reason` as words — no empty string, no zero, no
390	dash-without-meaning (the one dash with a meaning is the empty user belief, absence kind
391	`not_said`). *Test:* deltaRail › `test_renders_a_reason_for_every_absent_number`; **visual review
392	checklist line 5**.
393	
394	**INV-workbench.46 — the rail invents no order.** For every branch, while `ranked` is false the rail
395	renders the reachable terminals in the order the base map stores them, independent of every number
396	on the world. *Test:* deltaRail › `test_lists_reachable_terminals_in_map_order`.
397	
398	**INV-workbench.47 — how firm and same direction are never folded into the rank.** For every rail
399	row the two are rendered as their own columns, and no ordering function reads either. *Test:*
400	deltaRail › `test_never_sorts_by_width_or_agreement`.
401	
402	**INV-workbench.48 — a supposed claim shows the word.** For every claim under a live supposition,
403	the tile renders **Supposed · date** where a likelihood would go and renders no likelihood for it at
404	all; where a later edit undermined the supposition, both states render in order with the arrow
405	between them. *Test:* `frontend/src/components/__tests__/beliefChip.test.tsx` ›
406	`test_a_supposed_claim_renders_the_word_not_a_number`; **visual review checklist line 12**.
407	
408	**INV-workbench.49 — the branch is append-only and reads in vocabulary words.** For every sequence
409	of button presses, the branch is the edits in the order they were made with no earlier edit altered,
410	and every badge on screen is one of the six — the five in the *Interface words* table plus the
411	derived **Retracted · date · by "…"** — with no code name anywhere. *Tests:*
412	`frontend/src/world/__tests__/branchReducer.test.ts` ›
413	`test_appends_edits_in_order_and_never_rewrites_one`, `test_renders_only_interface_words`; **visual
414	review checklist line 11**.
415	
416	---
417	
418	## ANTI-PATTERNS
419	
420	1. **Do not commit a second set of numbers to make the diff look finished.** *Because* a number
421	   nobody computed cannot be traced to an input, a rule or a source — a veto condition — and once an
422	   illustrative world is in the tree everything downstream quietly believes it. **Instead:** ship the
423	   structure, which is real, and let every number slot render its absence with a reason.
424	
425	2. **Do not crossfade A into A′** — stated as an anti-pattern in
426	   [`color-motion-type.md`](color-motion-type.md), which owns motion. Here it means a hard switch on
427	   `Space`, scrubbable, both worlds always in the same coordinates.
428	
429	3. **Do not lay out A and A′ separately and place them side by side.** *Because* two layouts mean
430	   every tile moves a little, and a reader cannot tell a real change from a layout change.
431	   **Instead:** lay out the union once and paint into it twice.
432	
433	4. **Do not rank the delta rail before something has ranked it.** *Because* a ranking is a claim
434	   about which change matters most, and an invented one is a lie in the exact place the reader came
435	   for the truth. **Instead:** map order, visibly arbitrary, until the engine supplies its own.
436	
437	5. **Do not render a supposed claim as `1.0`, `.98`, `>.99` or a full bar.** *Because* a number
438	   invites the reader to wonder about the missing two per cent, and there is no such uncertainty.
439	   **Instead:** the word, and its date.
440	
441	6. **Do not let a button move a number in this stack, and do not rewrite an edit in place.**
442	   *Because* a canvas that computes its own likelihoods is a second engine, and two engines
443	   disagree; and because an edited history explains nothing. **Instead:** append an edit and let the
444	   number wait for the engine, saying so meanwhile.
445	
446	---
447	
448	## Open questions
449	
450	*Raised 2026-09-17. Four questions this chapter opened were settled by Kent the same day and now
451	read as statements in the body: which arrows carry a change (B2), what `killed` means (B2), which
452	columns the rail shows (B5), and what the one-line summary says when nothing moved (B5).*
453	
454	1. **Does the retraction badge need the world, or is the branch enough for good?** This stack derives
455	   it from the branch. Once the world carries the retraction, two derivations of one line exist, and
456	   one should become the only one — probably the world's. **Owner:** stack 04, when
457	   `ApiWorldSource` is switched on.
458
